description: Three distinct acts, deliberately held by three different parties. Collapsing any two of them removes the separation of duties that makes a release reversible and attributable.

release_approval.what: The CONTENT of the release is accepted: this change set, this migration plan, this rollback plan, these gate verdicts.
release_approval.who: release-manager assembles and recommends; a named human accepts.
release_approval.does_not_grant: Permission to deploy. An approved release may sit unapproved for production for a change window, a dependency, or a decision.

deployment_authorization.what: Production deployment of this approved release is PERMITTED, now.
deployment_authorization.who: The named release approver in .ai-engineering/project.yaml under approval.release_approver. A human, always.
deployment_authorization.does_not_grant: The ability to perform the deployment. Authorization and execution are different hands.

deployment_execution.who: devops-engineer, or CI acting on the authorization.
deployment_execution.artifact_state: REL moves authorized -> done after verification
deployment_execution.precondition: REL is in state 'authorized'. Executing against an 'approved' release that was never authorized is the failure this split exists to prevent.

verification.what: Confirming the deployed system behaves as the release said it would.
verification.who: release-manager with sre. Never the party that executed the deployment alone.
verification.artifact_state: REL moves authorized -> done, or -> rolled-back

separation_rules: release-manager recommends and verifies. It has no Bash and cannot deploy.
The human who authorizes is not the agent that assembled the release.
The party that executes the deployment does not also declare it verified.
A rollback is itself an authorized act: it needs the same human authorization as the deployment.
why_this_matters: In 0.2.0 approval and authorization were one act, so a release approved on Monday carried standing permission to deploy on Friday against a changed production. Separating them makes the authorization decision current.
